elements.evidence: "for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling"

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "and contractors and outsourcing providers acting on Sparkling's behalf"
Grant remains "a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use" with no perpetuity language.
No irrevocability wording added anywhere in the redlined grant.

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: No termination limitation inserted; clause is silent on grounds for revocation/termination.
"either party may assign this Agreement, together with the licence granted hereunder, without consent to a successor"
"affiliated companies of Sparkling ... operating at Authorized Locations" — covered outright, exceeding the notice-conditioned fallback

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "without consent to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

offending_extra_words: amalgamation, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business to which this Agreement relates
except as permitted by Section 20(d) or
reasons: Preferred level fails: no perpetual/irrevocable characterisation for paid-up licences and no limitation of termination/revocation to uncured material breach were added, so the locked preferred target is not achieved.

The fallback bargain is fully satisfied: affiliates are covered on the face of the grant (better than notice-conditioned coverage) and a consent-free assignment to an M&A successor now carries the licence.

Minimality fails: operation 1 nearly doubles the grant recital (14→25 words) and operation 3 expands an 8-word anchor into a 53-word proviso (changed-character ratio 0.861), where a short insertion such as 'and its contractors' plus a brief 'except to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets' would suffice.

'outsourcing providers' is surplus to 'contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf', and the four-way M&A enumeration plus 'or of the business to which this Agreement relates' is unnecessary boilerplate.

Intent is preserved: the Authorized Locations limit, additional-fee mechanic and mutual consent default remain effective, and the Section 20(d) cross-reference reconciles the retained 'non-transferable' grant with the new successor assignment right.
